subject: humanities
passage: In medieval Europe, books were often written on parchment, a material made from animal skin that was costly and slow to produce. When a book was no longer wanted, a scribe would sometimes scrape the ink off its pages and write a new text on the same parchment. Faint traces of the older writing often remained, and modern scientists have used special imaging to read them. As a result, some old parchment books ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: show no trace of the writing that was scraped off their pages.
choices.B: contain hidden texts older than the ones that can be seen on their pages.
choices.C: were copied onto paper by scribes before their pages were scraped.
choices.D: were scraped clean because parchment was cheap and easy to replace.

explanation.why: Scribes wrote new texts over scraped-off older ones, and traces of the older writing remained. Scientists can now read those traces, so some books hold an earlier text underneath the one that is visible.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says faint traces of the older writing often remained.
explanation.B: Correct. The scraped-off writing came first and still leaves traces under the newer text, so these books contain older, hidden texts.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never mentions copying old texts onto paper.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says parchment was costly and slow to produce, which is why it was reused.
